text: availability refers to accessibility and usability when required;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: confidentiality refers to access being restricted only to those authorised;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: criticality refers to the potential impact of a loss of availability;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: information asset means information and information technology, including software, hardware and data (both soft and hard copy);
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: information security means the preservation of an information asset’s confidentiality, integrity and availability;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: information security capability means the totality of resources, skills and controls which provide the ability and capacity to maintain information security;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: information security control means a prevention, detection or response measure to reduce the likelihood or impact of an information security incident;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: information security incident means an actual or potential compromise of information security;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: information security policy framework means the totality of policies, standards, guidelines and procedures pertaining to information security;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: information security threat (threat) is a circumstance or event that has the potential to exploit an information security vulnerability;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: information security vulnerability (vulnerability) is a weakness in an information asset or information security control that could be exploited to compromise information security;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: integrity refers to completeness, accuracy and freedom from unauthorised change or usage; and
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: sensitivity means the potential impact of a loss of confidentiality or integrity.
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: ‘group’ means a Level 2 group or a Level 3 group, as relevant;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: ‘Head of a group’ means a Level 2 Head or Level 3 Head, as relevant;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: ‘Level 2 group’ means the entities that comprise: (a) Level 2 as defined in APS 001; or (b) a Level 2 insurance group as defined in GPS 001;
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)

text: ‘Level 2 Head’ means: (a) where an ADI that is a member of a Level 2 group is not a subsidiary of an authorised banking NOHC or another ADI, that ADI; (b) where an ADI that is a member of a Level 2 group is a subsidiary of an authorised banking NOHC, that authorised banking NOHC; or (c) the parent entity of a Level 2 insurance group as defined in GPS 001.
source_document: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019)
